learningObjectives: Identify the key components of Pega application security including the AIC Triad, Security Checklist, and guardrail compliance.
Describe authentication vs. authorization and the three authorization models: RBAC, ABAC, and CBAC.

elements.text: Airport identity checks illustrate authentication; permission to enter particular areas illustrates authorization. A checklist tracks applicable security work before release. It is a process aid rather than proof that every possible attack has been prevented.

elements.description: Availability, Integrity, Confidentiality — Pega's shared security goal. Unauthorized individuals cannot access or modify the application or its data. Authorized individuals only access what they need to perform their jobs.

A guideline Rule instance automatically installed per app version to harden Pega applications. Tasks are organized by timing and key area: monitoring, authentication, authorization, auditing, production testing. Not all tasks are required for every app.

The source describes Deployment Manager blocking production promotion when the Security Checklist is incomplete. Applicable tasks depend on the application and deployment; not every listed task applies to every release.

The source emphasizes guardrail compliance because custom code can bypass built-in security enforcement. Use platform security features; do not treat compliance as a replacement for MFA, authorization design or security testing.

elements.description: Pega security operates at two distinct layers:
items: Application-level security: protects from outsiders and unauthorized users (passwords, auth policies, MFA, third-party tools)
Feature security: controls what authorized users can and cannot access within the app (RBAC, ABAC, CBAC)

elements.description: The earlier Security policies v5 source documents these navigation routes; v6 focuses on policy behavior. Verify the interface in the target version:
items: App Studio: Authentication landing page → Security Policies tab
Dev Studio: Configure → Org & Security → Authentication → Security Policies (applies to the entire Pega Platform server)
⚠ CAUTION: authentication service settings may OVERRIDE Security Policy page settings
Restrictions on predictable or reused passwords

elements.description: Presents a challenge on initial login or after failed login attempts. Can use a custom or default CAPTCHA.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Security Policies — Access Control and Monitoring

elements.description: Controls account lockout behavior after failed logins:
items: Enabled penalty: configure a failed-attempt threshold and initial seconds; repeat failures escalate the penalty.
Disabled penalty: configure failed-attempt count and lock duration in minutes. Disabling the penalty option does not mean all lockout protection disappears.

elements.description: Controls the level of detail recorded in the system log for security-related events.

The built-in OTP policy delivers a time-limited code by email or SMS. MFA is broader than this delivery mechanism; 2FA uses two factors. The source lists knowledge, possession and an inherent characteristic such as a fingerprint.
Automatically disables access for users who have been inactive for a specified number of days. An exclusion list can protect users who still require access despite inactivity.

elements.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 190" role="img" font-family="inherit"><title>Security policy responsibilities</title><rect x="10" y="10" width="740" height="170" rx="12" fill="var(--pa-surface)" stroke="var(--pa-brand)"/><text x="30" y="42" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="var(--pa-brand)">Security policy responsibilities</text><g font-size="14" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)"><text x="30" y="78">Password / CAPTCHA / Lockout: credential and login protection.</text><text x="30" y="110">Audit: login-event detail; OTP policy: additional evidence.</text><text x="30" y="142">Operator disablement: inactivity, with configured exclusions.</text></g></svg>
elements.caption: Security policy responsibilities.

elements.description: Authentication verifies identity for application and service access. An Operator ID is commonly an email address, but not necessarily one. SAML, OpenID Connect and token credentials support SSO; the authentication service configures applicable policies.
Controls what authenticated users can access and perform within the application. Three models: RBAC, ABAC, and CBAC.
RBAC assigns permissions through user Roles. It can complement other authorization models; it is not automatically sufficient for every security requirement.

Attribute-Based Access Control. Access is determined by comparing object characteristics (Case, field, document) to user attributes. More granular than RBAC — the same role can have different access depending on contextual attributes.
Client-Based Access Control. Tracks and processes requests to view, update, or remove personal customer data. Designed to address GDPR and similar data privacy regulations.

ABAC: object and requesting-user attributes.</text><text x="30" y="142">Client-Based Access Control: personal-data requests.</text></g></svg>

examPitfalls.title: AIC — correct order and acronym
examPitfalls.trapDescription: AIC names the same availability, integrity and confidentiality goals often called the CIA triad in another order; it is not a competing security model.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: AIC expands to Availability, Integrity, Confidentiality. Do not invent claims about certification question frequency.

examPitfalls.title: Security Checklist failure BLOCKS deployment — not just a warning
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A scenario asks what happens when Deployment Manager detects an incomplete Security Checklist. Candidates select 'generates a warning but deployment continues' — not knowing deployment is hard-blocked.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: In the described Deployment Manager process, complete applicable Checklist tasks before production promotion.

examPitfalls.title: Guardrail compliance is the #1 security requirement
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Guardrail compliance supports enforcement but does not replace the other security controls.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Guardrail compliance is the most important requirement. Pega's security features may not work correctly when custom code is used — always use built-in Pega security.

examPitfalls.title: Auth service settings can OVERRIDE Security Policies page settings
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question describes conflicting values between Auth service and the Security Policies page, asking which wins. Candidates assume Security Policies page always takes precedence — Auth service settings can override it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Settings configured for a specific authentication service may OVERRIDE the Security Policies page settings — always check auth service configuration.

examPitfalls.title: 2FA is a SUBSET of MFA — not the same thing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: An exam question asks whether 2FA and MFA are equivalent. Candidates select 'Yes — they require the same number of factors.' MFA is the broader category (two OR more); 2FA is a specific subset requiring exactly two.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Two-factor authentication (2FA) requires exactly two evidence factors — it is a subset of MFA. MFA is the broader category requiring two or more factors.

examPitfalls.title: ABAC vs. CBAC — different purposes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Here CBAC means Client-Based Access Control, not Class-Based or Claim-Based. It addresses personal-data requests; ABAC evaluates attributes.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: CBAC tracks personal-data requests. It supports a privacy process; selecting it does not by itself establish regulatory compliance.

examPitfalls.title: Security Policies navigation: App Studio ≠ Dev Studio path
examPitfalls.trapDescription: An exam question asks for the Dev Studio navigation path to Security Policies. Candidates describe the App Studio path (Authentication landing page → Security Policies tab) and lose marks for swapping the two paths.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: These routes are documented in Security policies v5. Confirm navigation against the target interface rather than assuming all versions use the same route.

quickRecap.value: Availability, Integrity, Confidentiality — the same goals often ordered CIA.
Track applicable security tasks; the described Deployment Manager promotion gate requires completion.
Maintain built-in enforcement through guardrail compliance; use it alongside other security controls.
Password, CAPTCHA, Lockout (penalty grows), Audit (log detail), MFA (OTP email/SMS), Operator disablement (inactive users).
Security policies v5 documents App Studio Authentication → Security Policies and Dev Studio Configure → Org & Security → Authentication → Security Policies. Verify target-version UI.
Specific auth service settings may OVERRIDE Security Policies page settings.
2FA is a SUBSET of MFA. MFA = two or more factors. 2FA = exactly two.
Authentication = WHO can access (Operator ID + password; SSO: SAML 2.0/OpenID Connect/tokens). Authorization = WHAT they can do.
RBAC (job roles), ABAC (object attributes vs user attributes), CBAC (personal data / GDPR compliance).
